selectedAnswer.answer:
GlossBERT constructs context-gloss pairs from glosses of all possible senses of the target word in WordNet, treating WSD as a sentence-pair classification problem. [1][2]
For each target word, glosses of all N possible senses are extracted to form the gloss sentence; the record gives N=4 as an example. [3]
[CLS] and [SEP] marks are added to the context-gloss pairs to make them suitable as input to the BERT model. [4]
At test time, the probability of label=yes is output for each context-gloss pair, and the sense with the highest probability is chosen as the prediction. [5]

selectedAnswer.answer:
The proposed BERT-based natural language generation model can be trained end-to-end without handcrafted features. [1]
The model uses a two-stage decoder process, generating each summary word using context information from both sides. [2]
During model training, the objective is the sum of the two processes, jointly trained using the teacher-forcing algorithm, with ground-truth summaries fed to each decoder. [3]
The model loss is defined as the sum of the decoder loss and the refine loss (L_model = L_dec + L_refine). [4]
BERT is used on both the encoder and decoder of the seq2seq model. [5]
Training used the Adam optimizer with learning rate 3e-4, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, epsilon=1e-9, and a dynamic learning rate. [6]
Training used batch size 36 for 4 epochs (8 epochs for NYT50), with the best model selected from the last 10 models based on development set performance. [7]
